text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Environmental protection is being made a component of all national economic planning between now and 2000.
-- Sweden's International Development Cooperation Agency will provide $400,000 to help Hanoi preserve and develop its old quarter.
-- Vietnam will import between 600,000-650,000 tonnes of wheat flour annually by 2000.
-- The Central Economic Management Institute has proposed measures aimed at improving the managerial role of state enterprises in joint-ventures with foreign partners.
-- Some 4.5 tons of gold bars worth more than $50 million have been imported into Ho Chi Minh City through border gates so far this year.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has told the German ambassador that economic and investment cooperation between the two countries should be further strengthened.
-- Vietnam exported more than 2,000 tonnes of tea in the first five months of this year, a three-fold increase from the same period last year.
-- Vietnam sold 70 billion dong ($6.0 million) worth of one year Treasury notes with an annual coupon of 11.9 percent on Wednesday.
-- More than one hundred people involved in drug-related crimes were tried by courts in Hanoi in May.
-- Vietnam's first compact disc factory started operations last week. The factory will produce 6 million CD's each year.
